acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
guide_faults: The skill teaches placement/shape/index discipline thoroughly but never instructs the writer to verify a mechanism doc's technical claims against the actual shipped code first; for a layer whose whole premise is 'must change with the code it describes,' that's a load-bearing gap. It shows: the with-guide doc confidently describes a token-bucket algorithm split across three files (a project a file, a file) and an external-store option and a Retry-After header — none of which exist in the real a server file (fixed-window counter, single file, IP-only key via x-forwarded-for, X-RateLimit-* headers, no Retry-After, in-process Map only, no external store). Faithfully following the guide's shape produced a doc that is fluent and wrong.

The seeded worked example (templates/live-doc-example.md) is a bare four-section skeleton for a trivial one-function mechanism; this project's own existing mechanism docs (e.g. the mechanism doc) have already evolved past it — tables, cross-links to specs and BACKLOG gap files, inline caveats about known hardening gaps. The guide gives no signal for when a mechanism has outgrown the toy shape, so literal imitation (which the guide explicitly prescribes via its own 'delete the seeded example once a real mechanism exists' step) yields a page thinner than the house norm it's supposed to match.
acceptance.verdict: Guide won cleanly on structure — correct mechanism-vs-ADR-vs-skill placement, exact seeded shape, correct no-duplicate-index restraint, checkable update-trigger — versus a padded, generically-shaped isolated baseline; but neither agent grounded the doc in the real code, and the with-guide output stated specific wrong implementation details (token-bucket, files that don't exist) with more unearned confidence than the baseline's honest hedging.

checklist.note: No text steering the reading model; content is standard/prose, no embedded directives.
No network sends of repo/user data; only a documented gh api fetch of the installer itself.
No keys, tokens, or credentials present in SKILL.md or sources.md.
No destructive shell commands run; only a documented bash <(gh api ...) install one-liner the user must invoke themselves.
No base64/hex payloads or eval of decoded blobs; all content is plain readable prose/markdown.
documented user-invoked installer (bash <(gh api ...) from the marketplace repo); the skill does not execute it itself
No reference to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, or cookie stores; only requires gh to already be authenticated.
No sudo, setuid, or persistence via cron/shell-profile/launch-agent edits.
